title: Corp as aigney
description: Ten short stories about the body and the mind on the Isle of Man: a javelin thrower's lungs, a boy learning to say his sounds, a twisted foot on a valley walk, a worker's back, a harpist at an inn, a lecture on a novel about memory, a centre for mental health, healthy Manx food, the bones of an extinct deer in the museum, and a night of revision before a science exam.

lessons.title: Y roortagh as e scowanyn
lessons.summary: Thaddeus Ravenscroft, a javelin thrower in Douglas, has trouble breathing three weeks before a big competition; the nurse Philomena Gilchrist does a lung test, the doctor gives him bad news and medicine, and after his disappointment he gets his strength back and wins in Scotland in the winter.
lessons.text:
Ta Thaddeus Ravenscroft ny roortagh. T'eh kiare bleeaney as feed d'eash, as t'eh cummal ayns Doolish. She ceau y sleean yn spoyrt echey. Dagh moghrey, ta Thaddeus goll dys y pairk, as t'eh ceau y sleean keead keayrt. Ta'n sleean echey liauyr. Ta ram roortee firryn ayns y chlub echey, agh she Thaddeus y roortagh share.

'Sy tourey shoh, va Thaddeus goll dys roortys mooar ayns Sostyn. Agh three shiaghtinyn roish y roortys, va doilleeid echey lesh e ennal. Tra v'eh roie, cha row eh abyl ennal y ghoaill dy mie. Hie eh dys y fer-lhee.

“Lhisagh oo goll dys y thie-lheeys son teisht scowanagh,” dooyrt y fer-lhee. “Ta mee laccal fakin cre'n aght ta ny scowanyn ayd gobbraghey.”

'Sy thie-lheeys, va boandyr aeg, Philomena Gilchrist, jeeaghyn lurg Thaddeus. Ren Philomena y teisht scowanagh. Va er Thaddeus ennal mooar y ghoaill, as eisht yn ennal y lhiggey magh ayns jeshaght beg, reesht as reesht. “Ta'n teisht shoh soit er ny scowanyn ayd,” dooyrt y boandyr. “Lhig magh dty ennal dy lajer, as dy liauyr.”

Lurg y teisht, haink y fer-lhee. “Cha nel y naight aym mie,” dooyrt eh. “Ta çhingys scowanagh ort.”

“Vel eh olk?” denee Thaddeus.

“Cha nel eh feer olk,” dooyrt y fer-lhee, “agh cha bee oo ayns y roortys shoh.”

Va molley mooar er Thaddeus. Va'n roortys shoh feer scanshoil da. “Ta mee er ve gobbraghey son y roortys shoh rish blein slane,” dooyrt eh rish Philomena. “Ta'n molley shoh ro vooar.”

Hug y fer-lhee medshin da. “Gow y medshin shoh dagh moghrey as dagh fastyr,” dooyrt eh. “Lesh y medshin, bee ny scowanyn ayd lajer reesht.”

“Ta molley ort nish,” dooyrt y boandyr, “agh ta roortys elley ayn 'sy gheurey. Bee oo lajer son shen.”

Ghow Thaddeus y medshin dagh laa. Lurg mee, va bioys noa ayn. V'eh roie reesht, as v'eh ceau y sleean ny sodjey na roie. Va'n bioys shen ry-akin ayns dagh red v'eh jannoo. Ayns y gheurey, hie eh dys y roortys elley ayns Nalbin. Cheau eh y sleean ny sodjey na dagh roortagh firryn elley, as hooar eh y chied ynnyd.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n spoyrt ta ec Thaddeus?
She ceau y sleean yn spoyrt echey.
Quoi ren y teisht scowanagh?
Ren y boandyr, Philomena Gilchrist, y teisht scowanagh.
Row'n çhingys scowanagh olk?
Cha row. Cha row eh feer olk, agh cha row Thaddeus abyl goll dys y roortys ayns Sostyn.
Cre hug y fer-lhee da?
Hug eh medshin da.
Cre haghyr da Thaddeus lurg mee?
Va bioys noa ayn, as v'eh roie reesht.
Cre haghyr ayns Nalbin?
Cheau Thaddeus y sleean ny sodjey na dagh roortagh firryn elley, as hooar eh y chied ynnyd.

lessons.title: Barnabas as ny corocklyn
lessons.summary: Five-year-old Barnabas Underwood in Ramsey cannot say r and l, so his mother Octavia takes him to the speech teacher Cordelia Wainwright: she transcribes his speech, finds a phonological problem with the approximants, explains the terms and the soft palate, works with gentleness and sensory games, and after some months people understand him.
lessons.text:
Ta Barnabas Underwood queig bleeaney d'eash. T'eh cummal marish e voir, Octavia, ayns Rhumsaa. Ta Barnabas loayrt dy mennick as dy ard, agh cha nel sleih elley toiggal eh dy mie. Cha nel eh abyl gra kuse dy chorocklyn, as ta ny focklyn echey goll cam. Ta e voir toiggal y loayrtys echey, agh cha nel ny paitçhyn elley 'sy scoill toiggal eh. Ta toiggalys y loayrtys echey ro veg.

Er-y-fa shen, hie Octavia lesh Barnabas dys Cordelia Wainwright. She ynseyder loayrtys ee. T'ee gobbraghey lesh paitçhyn nagh vel loayrt dy mie.

Hoshiaght, ren Cordelia loayrt rish Barnabas son tammylt, as ren ee coontey jeh'n loayrtys echey. Eisht ren ee aascreeu sheeanagh jeh ny focklyn echey. Ayns yn aascreeu, ta lettyr er lheh son dagh sheean. Hoilshee Cordelia yn aascreeu da Octavia. “Jeeagh,” dooyrt ee. “Tra ta Barnabas gra ‘lioar’, ta'n aascreeu soilshaghey nagh vel y chied corockle kiart.”

“Cre'n doilleeid t'ayn?” denee Octavia.

“She doilleeid sheeanchoryssagh t'ayn,” dooyrt Cordelia. “Cha nel ny feeacklyn ny'n chengey echey olk. Ta'n doilleeid sheeanchoryssagh ayns y corys sheean echey. Ta Barnabas gra dagh corockle cadjin dy mie, agh cha nel eh gra yn faggyssaght dy mie. She faggyssaght ta ayns y chied corockle jeh ‘lioar’, as ayns y chied corockle jeh ‘ree’ myrgeddin. She ‘faggyssaght’ yn termeeaght son corockle raad ta'n chengey çheet faggys da mullagh y veeal, as ta'n aer goll magh dy aashagh. Ta ram termeeaght ec ynseyderyn loayrtys, agh cha nel feme ayd er y termeeaght ooilley.”

Hoilshee Cordelia daue jalloo jeh'n veeal. “Shoh y chengey, as shoh ny feeacklyn. Ec cooyl y veeal, shoh yn clea. Ta'n clea goll seose tra ta shin gra kuse dy chorocklyn. Ta'n clea mie ec Barnabas.”

Va Cordelia gobbraghey lesh Barnabas dagh shiaghtin. Va meenid vooar eck. Cha row ee rieau loayrt dy ard rish, as cha row aggle rieau er Barnabas. Ren ee loayrt rish lesh meenid, as ren eh gearey dy mennick. Ren ee ymmyd jeh cloieyn keeallagh: va Barnabas bentyn da'n veeal echey, jeeaghyn er e chengey hene, as goaill blass jeh reddyn mollagh as millish. Ta cloieyn keeallagh mie son paitçhyn beggey.

Lurg shey meeaghyn, va Barnabas abyl gra “lioar” as “ree” dy kiart. Ren Cordelia aascreeu noa jeh'n loayrtys echey, as va dagh sheean kiart. Nish ta ny paitçhyn elley toiggal eh, as ta toiggalys y loayrtys echey mie.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n doilleeid va ec Barnabas?
Cha row eh abyl gra kuse dy chorocklyn, as cha row toiggalys y loayrtys echey mie.
Cre'n doilleeid va ayns y loayrtys echey, rere Cordelia?
She doilleeid sheeanchoryssagh v'ayn.
Cre ren Cordelia jeh ny focklyn echey?
Ren ee aascreeu sheeanagh jeh ny focklyn echey.
Cre'n termeeaght son y chied corockle jeh “lioar”?
She faggyssaght yn termeeaght son y corockle shen.
Cre'n aght va Cordelia loayrt rish Barnabas?
Va Cordelia loayrt rish lesh meenid.
Cre ren Cordelia ymmyd jeh?
Ren ee ymmyd jeh cloieyn keeallagh.

lessons.title: Shooyl 'sy strah
lessons.summary: Leopold Merriweather and his wife Hyacinth walk up a broad wooded valley in the north despite a forecast of showers; they go through a gap in a wall and down stone steps, Leopold, whose shoes have little grip, slips into a hollow and twists his foot, Hyacinth ties a tight cloth round it, and they walk home slowly.
lessons.text:
Ta Leopold Merriweather as e ven, Hyacinth, cummal ayns Sulby. S'mie lhieu shooyl, as dagh Jesarn t'ad goll er shooyl. Er y Jesarn shoh, v'ad laccal goll seose y strah mooar ry-lhiattee rish y valley. She strah lheead t'ayn, as ta awin goll trooid. Er dagh çheu jeh'n strah, ta ny sleityn billagh: ta biljyn ayns dy chooilley voayl. Ta Hyacinth gra dy nee'n strah billagh shoh yn ynnyd s'aalin 'sy twoaie.

“Ta'n emshir goll dy ve fliugh jiu,” dooyrt Hyacinth, as ee jeeaghyn er y çhellveeish. “Ta frassaghey trome çheet 'sy lhiurid y laa.”

“Cha nel aggle orrym roish frassaghey,” dooyrt Leopold. “Ta cooat mie aym.”

Hie ad magh. Va glasseraght ard ry-lhiattee rish y raad. Va'n glasseraght shoh glass as aalin, agh va'n raad beg as fliugh. Va Hyacinth gra ennym dagh lus 'sy glasseraght. Haink y chied frassaghey, as va ny biljyn ayns y strah billagh fliugh. Lurg tammylt, haink ad gys boalley clagh. Va baarney ayns y voalley, as hie ad trooid y baarney. Ec y çheu elley jeh'n baarney, va greeishyn clagh goll sheese gys yn awin.

Va ny greeishyn fliugh lurg y frassaghey. Va braagyn noa ec Hyacinth, as va ny braagyn eck greimmagh. Va braagyn shenn ec Leopold, as cha row ny braagyn echey greimmagh dy liooar. Er y greeish s'jerree, huitt Leopold. Huitt eh ayns slogh beg ry-lhiattee rish yn awin. Va'n slogh lane dy ushtey as dy laagh.

Chammee Leopold e chass ayns y slogh. “Cha nel mee abyl shassoo er my chass!” dooyrt eh. Va mwannal e chass goll mooar.

Va eaddagh ec Hyacinth. Hug ee yn eaddagh mygeayrt mwannal e chass, as ren ee kiangley jeen. “T'eh jeen dy liooar,” dooyrt Leopold. “Cha nel eh gleashagh nish.”

Hie ad erash dy moal. Hie ad seose ny greeishyn, as trooid y baarney reesht. Va Leopold goaill greim er laue Hyacinth. Lurg three oor, v'ad ec y thie. Ren Hyacinth tey son Leopold.

“Ny jean shooyl ayns ny braagyn shenn shen reesht,” dooyrt ee. “Cha nel ad greimmagh. Kionnee braagyn noa.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad hie Leopold as Hyacinth er shooyl?
Hie ad seose y strah mooar ry-lhiattee rish Sulby.
Cre dooyrt Hyacinth mychione yn emshir?
Dooyrt ee dy row frassaghey trome çheet.
Cre'n aght hie ad trooid y voalley?
Hie ad trooid baarney ayns y voalley.
Cre'n fa huitt Leopold?
Huitt eh er-y-fa nagh row ny braagyn echey greimmagh dy liooar.
Cre haghyr da cass Leopold?
Chammee eh e chass ayns y slogh.
Cre ren Hyacinth?
Hug ee eaddagh mygeayrt mwannal e chass, as ren ee kiangley jeen.

lessons.title: Y disc ayns dreeym Ignatius
lessons.summary: Ignatius Pickering, a worker in a Peel boatyard, hurts his back lifting steel; he fears cancer, which killed his father, but the doctor Seraphina Lancaster says the apparent cause is a disc, a scan confirms it, and he sticks to his exercises and pays the cost of a few sessions himself.
lessons.text:
Ta Ignatius Pickering ny labree ayns thie troggal lhongyn ayns Pheeil. T'eh jeih bleeaney as daeed d'eash. Ta'n obbyr echey trome. Ta ny labreeyn troggal lhongyn veih fuygh as veih staillin. Dagh laa, ta Ignatius troggal peeshyn trome jeh staillin.

Un moghrey, va Ignatius troggal peesh vooar jeh staillin, as haink doilleeid ayns e ghreeym. Cha row eh abyl shassoo seose. Hug labreeyn elley eh thie 'sy ghleashtan.

Va aggle er Ignatius. Ghow yn ayr echey baase jeh kanghyr roish jeih bleeaney, as va'n kanghyr shen ayns y dreeym echey ec y toshiaght. “Vel kanghyr orrym myrgeddin?” va Ignatius smooinaghtyn.

Hie eh dys y fer-lhee, Seraphina Lancaster. Dinsh eh di mychione e ayr as y kanghyr. Eisht ren ee jeeaghyn er y dreeym echey.

“She disc t'ayn, er-lhiam,” dooyrt ee. “Ta disc ayns y dreeym eddyr dagh craue. Tra ta dooinney troggal red ro hrome, ta disc gleashagh ny keayrtyn. Shen yn oyr baghtagh. Ta'n oyr baghtagh dy liooar, agh lhisagh shin fondaghey eh. Hed oo dys y thie-lheeys son jalloo jeh dty ghreeym.”

Lurg shiaghtin, hooar Seraphina y jalloo. Ren y jalloo fondaghey ny dooyrt Seraphina: va disc er ghleashagh. Cha row kanghyr erbee ayn. “Ta'n jalloo er fondaghey shen,” dooyrt Seraphina. “Cha nel kanghyr ort.” Va Ignatius booiagh dy liooar.

“Lhisagh oo gleashaghtyn er lheh y yannoo dagh laa,” dooyrt Seraphina. “Lhisagh oo lhiantyn rish ny gleashaghtyn shoh son three meeaghyn. My vees oo lhiantyn roo, bee'n dreeym ayd lajer reesht.”

Hug ee lioar veg da lesh jallooyn jeh ny gleashaghtyn. Va Ignatius lhiantyn rish ny gleashaghtyn dagh moghrey as dagh fastyr. Hie eh myrgeddin dys ben ta gobbraghey lesh sleih lesh doilleeidyn 'sy dreeym. Va costys ayn: va dagh oor feed punt. Va'n costys ard, agh va Ignatius booiagh dy eeck eh. “Ta'n costys mooar,” dooyrt eh rish e ven, “agh ta'n dreeym aym ny smoo scanshoil na'n argid.”

Lurg three meeaghyn, va Ignatius erash ec y thie troggal lhongyn. Nish t'eh troggal staillin dy moal, lesh e chassyn as cha nee lesh e ghreeym.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n obbyr ta ec Ignatius?
T'eh ny labree ayns thie troggal lhongyn ayns Pheeil.
Cre'n fa va aggle er Ignatius?
Va aggle er er-y-fa dy ghow e ayr baase jeh kanghyr.
Cre va'n oyr baghtagh, rere Seraphina?
She disc va'n oyr baghtagh.
Cre ren y jalloo fondaghey?
Ren y jalloo fondaghey dy row disc er ghleashagh, as nagh row kanghyr ayn.
Cre'n costys va ayn son dagh oor?
Va'n costys feed punt son dagh oor.

lessons.title: Y chlaasagh 'sy thie oastagh
lessons.summary: For ten years the harpist Marguerite Ellsworth has played on Friday nights at Fabian Hargreaves's inn in Laxey; after a cammag match against a neighbouring village the fans of both sides fill the inn, she plays for them, the host praises her, and she says she thinks music is good for the mind.
lessons.text:
Ta Marguerite Ellsworth cloie y chlaasagh. Dagh Jeheiney, t'ee cloie y chlaasagh ayns thie oastagh beg ayns Laksaa. She Fabian Hargreaves yn oastagh. T'eh er ve ny oastagh ayns y thie shoh rish feed blein. Ta'n oastagh mie rish dy chooilley pheiagh ta çheet stiagh.

She yn jeihoo blein eck ayns y thie oastagh shoh. Ghow ee toshiaght dy chloie ayn roish jeih bleeaney. Ayns y chied vlein, cha row agh three ny kiare persoonyn clashtyn rish. Nish, ayns y jeihoo blein, ta'n thie lane dagh Jeheiney. She'n chlaasagh yn eunysseyrys share ayns Laksaa, rere ny sleih.

Er y Jesarn shoh, va cloie cammag ayn. She shenn chloie yn ellan t'ayn ayns cammag, as ta lorg as bluckan ec ny cloiederyn. Va fwirran Laksaa cloie noi fwirran veih balley gerroil. Ta'n daa valley gerroil rish y cheilley, as ta ny fwirranyn oc nyn noidyn shenn ayns cammag.

Va ram graihderyn ec dagh fwirran. Va graihderyn Laksaa ayns jiarg, as va graihderyn y valley gerroil ayns gorrym. Va'n chloie cammag feer vie, as ren fwirran Laksaa barriaght. Lurg y chloie, haink ny graihderyn ooilley stiagh 'sy thie oastagh.

“Cha nel mee er vakin wheesh dy leih ayns y thie rieau,” dooyrt yn oastagh rish Marguerite. “Ta feme oc er eunysseyrys.”

Ren Marguerite cloie y chlaasagh. Hoshiaght, va ny graihderyn loayrt dy ard, agh lurg tammylt, v'ad clashtyn rish. Ren ee shenn arraneyn yn ellan y chloie, as ren ny graihderyn goaill ny arraneyn marish. Va graihderyn jiarg as graihderyn gorrym goaill arraneyn ry-cheilley.

'Sy jerrey, va Marguerite moyllit liorish yn oastagh roish dagh peiagh. “Lhig da'n ven shoh ve moyllit,” dooyrt eh. “Rish jeih bleeaney, t'ee er chur eunysseyrys dooin ooilley.” Va ny focklyn echey feer voyllagh, as va Marguerite moyllit liorish ny graihderyn myrgeddin.

“Ta mee sheiltyn dy vel kiaull mie son yn aigney,” dooyrt Marguerite rish yn oastagh. “Tra ta sleih loayrt dy ard as dy olk, ta kiaull cur shee orroo. Ta mee sheiltyn dy row shen ry-akin er yn oie shoh.”

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta Marguerite cloie y chlaasagh?
T'ee cloie y chlaasagh ayns thie oastagh ayns Laksaa.
Quoi yn oastagh?
She Fabian Hargreaves yn oastagh.
Cre wheesh bleeaney t'ee er ve cloie ayns y thie oastagh?
T'ee er ve cloie ayn rish jeih bleeaney. She yn jeihoo blein eck ayns y thie oastagh.
Quoi va cloie cammag noi Laksaa?
Va fwirran veih balley gerroil cloie noi Laksaa.
Cre haghyr 'sy jerrey?
Va Marguerite moyllit liorish yn oastagh roish dagh peiagh.
Cre ta Marguerite sheiltyn mychione kiaull?
T'ee sheiltyn dy vel kiaull mie son yn aigney.

lessons.title: Leaght mychione noaskeeal
lessons.summary: Clementine Ogden, a student of Manx in Douglas, goes to a lecture by the scholar Peregrine Sutcliffe on an old novel whose narrator has lost part of his memory: he explains the narrator's conditional verbs and intransitive verbs, the literary language and the biographical side of the book, and afterwards she finds it in the library catalogue.
lessons.text:
Ta Clementine Ogden nuy bleeaney jeig d'eash, as t'ee ynsaghey Gaelg ec y cholleish ayns Doolish. Er y Jerdein shoh, hie ee dys leaght ayns y lioarlann. Va'n leaght mychione screeudeyrys ayns Gaelg. Va schoillar mooar, Peregrine Sutcliffe, ginsh y leaght. She schoillar screeudeyrys eh, as t'eh er ve jannoo studeyrys er screeudeyrys yn ellan rish daeed blein.

Va'n leaght mychione shenn noaskeeal. Ayns y noaskeeal, ta'n insheyder ny shenn dooinney. T'eh er choayl ayrn jeh e chooinaghtyn. Ta'n insheyder ginsh mychione e aegid, agh cha nel eh shickyr jeh dy chooilley red.

“Jeeagh er ny breearyn ta'n insheyder jannoo ymmyd jeu,” dooyrt y schoillar. “Ta ram breearyn kianglagh ayn: ‘veagh’, ‘yinnin’, ‘harragh’. Cha nel yn insheyder gra ‘va mee ayns y thie’. T'eh gra ‘veagh mee ayns y thie, er-lhiam’. Ta'n emshir kianglagh soilshaghey nagh vel eh shickyr jeh ny cooinaghtyn echey.”

Eisht loayr y schoillar mychione breearyn neuchaghlaaee. “Ta breear neuchaghlaaee gyn red ta goll er,” dooyrt eh. “‘Hie eh’, ‘haink eh’, ‘huitt eh’: ta ny breearyn shoh neuchaghlaaee. Ayns y noaskeeal, ta'n insheyder jannoo ymmyd jeh breearyn neuchaghlaaee son y chooid smoo. Ta reddyn taghyrt da, agh cha nel eh hene jannoo red erbee da sleih elley.”

Ren Clementine screeu dy chooilley red ayns e lioar.

“Ta'n çhengey ayns y noaskeeal focklymagh,” dooyrt Peregrine. “Cha nel ee cadjin. Ta'n screeudeyr screeu ayns Gaelg focklymagh, as ny keayrtyn t'ee doillee da lhaihderyn noa. Agh ta'n insheyder hene loayrt ayns Gaelg cadjin. Shen yn oyr dy vel y lioar cho aalin. Ta'n Ghaelg focklymagh as y Ghaelg cadjin ry-cheilley ayn.”

'Sy jerrey, loayr y schoillar mychione bea y screeudeyr. “Ta'n noaskeeal beashnyssagh, ayns ayrn,” dooyrt eh. “Ren ayr y screeudeyr coayl e chooinaghtyn tra v'eh shenn. Ta ayrn beashnyssagh 'sy lioar, agh she skeeal t'ayn chammah.”

Lurg y leaght, hie Clementine dys y catalog 'sy lioarlann. Ren ee shirrey yn noaskeeal 'sy catalog er y cho-earrooder. Va'n lioar ayns y catalog, as va ee 'sy lioarlann. Ghow Clementine y lioar thie, as ren ee toshiaght dy lhaih ee er yn oie cheddin.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ren ginsh y leaght?
Ren y schoillar, Peregrine Sutcliffe, ginsh y leaght.
Cre'n sorçh dooinney yn insheyder ayns y noaskeeal?
She shenn dooinney yn insheyder, as t'eh er choayl ayrn jeh e chooinaghtyn.
Cre'n fa ta'n insheyder jannoo ymmyd jeh breearyn kianglagh?
Er-y-fa nagh vel eh shickyr jeh ny cooinaghtyn echey.
Vel y noaskeeal beashnyssagh?
Ta, ayns ayrn. Ren ayr y screeudeyr coayl e chooinaghtyn.
C'raad hooar Clementine y lioar?
Hooar ee y lioar 'sy catalog 'sy lioarlann.

lessons.title: Thie son slaynt yn aigney
lessons.summary: The government plans a new centre for mental health on farmland in an old treen near Jurby; at a meeting led by the Reverend Alaric Cartwright there is local opposition, but the election candidate Beatrix Rutherford explains that the old hospital has too little capacity, talks about diversity and a small principality that has such a centre, and a messenger brings a letter that settles the plan.
lessons.text:
Ta'n reiltys laccal thie noa y hroggal son sleih lesh çhingys yn aigney. She ynnyd beg t'ayn, lesh shiaght thieyn beggey as garey mooar. Ta'n reiltys laccal troggal y thie er magher ayns shenn treen faggys da Jurby. Ta treen ny ayrn shenn jeh'n thalloo ayns Ellan Vannin. Ta mysh 180 treen 'syn ellan, as ta keeill veg ayns ram treen.

Ta condaigys ayn noi'n thie noa. Ta kuse dy leih ayns y treen gra nagh vel ad laccal y thie. Er-y-fa shen, va quaiyl mooar ayn ayns thie y valley. Ren yn Arrymagh Alaric Cartwright, saggyrt y skylley, y quaiyl y leeid.

“Ta shin ayns shoh dy loayrt mychione y thie noa,” dooyrt yn Arrymagh. “Ta condaigys ayn, as lhisagh shin clashtyn rish y chondaigys. Agh lhisagh shin clashtyn rish dy chooilley pheiagh.”

Loayr eirinagh shenn hoshiaght. “Ta mee cummal 'sy treen shoh rish my vea,” dooyrt eh. “Ta aggle orrym. Cha nel fys aym quoi vees cummal ayns y thie shoh.”

Eisht loayr Beatrix Rutherford. She yeearreyder ee ayns y reihys ta çheet. T'ee er ve ny boandyr ayns y thie-lheeys ayns Doolish rish feed blein. “Ta'n shenn thie-lheeys son slaynt yn aigney ro veg,” dooyrt y yeearreyder. “Cha nel cummys dy liooar ayn. Ta cummys ayn son daeed persoon, agh ta feme ec queig as three feed persoon er. Ta sleih laccal ynnyd, as cha nel ad geddyn ynnyd son meeaghyn.”

“Ta caghlaays mooar mastey ny sleih shoh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta mraane as deiney, sleih aegey as sleih shenn, eirinee as fir-obbyr ayns shappyn ayn. Ta'n caghlaays shoh 'sy pobble ooilley, as ta'n caghlaays mie. Cha lhisagh aggle ve orrin roue.”

Dinsh y yeearreyder daue mychione Monaco. “She prinsaght veg ee Monaco, as t'ee ny sloo na Ellan Vannin,” dooyrt ee. “Ta thie myr shoh ec y phrinsaght shen, as t'ad gra dy vel eh mie son y phrinsaght ooilley.”

Tra va'n quaiyl er jerrey, haink chaghter stiagh lesh lettyr veih'n reiltys. Va'n chaghter feer aeg, as va'n lettyr echey ayns e laue. Lhaih yn Arrymagh y lettyr dy ard: va'n reiltys cur argid son y thie noa, as va'n cummys goll dy ve daa cheayrt cho mooar.

Cha row y chondaigys ooilley er jerrey, agh va ram sleih booiagh.

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta'n reiltys laccal troggal y thie noa?
Ta'n reiltys laccal troggal y thie er magher ayns shenn treen faggys da Jurby.
Quoi ren y quaiyl y leeid?
Ren yn Arrymagh Alaric Cartwright y quaiyl y leeid.
Cre dooyrt y yeearreyder mychione y shenn thie-lheeys?
Dooyrt ee nagh row cummys dy liooar ayn.
Cre'n sorçh dy heer ee Monaco?
She prinsaght veg ee Monaco.
Quoi haink stiagh lesh lettyr?
Haink chaghter aeg stiagh lesh lettyr veih'n reiltys.

lessons.title: Bee noa son cree Evander
lessons.summary: After a heart scare, Evander Thistlethwaite in Peel must eat better, so his wife Ophelia turns to old Manx cookery: herring from the harbour, where his grandfather worked in the herring fishery, raw green vegetables, apple juice, oval grapes ripening on the vine that Evander waters in the greenhouse, and eggs whose shells go on the garden.
lessons.text:
Ta Evander Thistlethwaite daa vlein as three feed d'eash, as t'eh cummal ayns Pheeil marish e ven, Ophelia. 'Sy tourey, va doilleeid echey lesh e chree, as hie eh dys y thie-lheeys. “Cha nel dty chree feer olk,” dooyrt y fer-lhee, “agh lhisagh oo bee share y ee. Ta ro vooar dy hollan ayns dty vee.”

Ren Ophelia smooinaghtyn mychione shen. “Lhig dooin goll erash gys shenn choagyraght Ellan Vannin,” dooyrt ee. “Va coagyraght Ellan Vannin aashagh as mie, as va sleih lajer. Va ny sleih ee eeast, praaseyn as glassrey.”

Ayns y choagyraght shen, va ram skeddan. Hoshiaght, ren Ophelia skeddan y chionnaghey ec y phurt. Ta'n skeddan ny eeast beg, as t'eh mie son y chree. Rish keeadyn dy vleeantyn, va eeasteyraght y skeddan feer scanshoil ayns Pheeil. Va shenn ayr Evander ny eeasteyr, as v'eh gobbraghey 'sy eeasteyraght rish e vea. “Ayns laghyn my henn ayr, va keead baatey ayns y phurt son yn eeasteyraght,” dooyrt Evander. “Nish cha nel agh beggan.”

Eisht, ren Ophelia toshiaght dy chur glassrey aw er y voayrd. Va duillagyn eayney ayn, as cabbag eayney myrgeddin. “Ta glassrey aw ny share na glassrey çheh,” dooyrt ee. Cha row Evander laccal glassrey aw y ee ec y toshiaght, agh lurg shiaghtin, va mian echey er y glassrey eayney.

Va soolagh ooyl er y voayrd dagh moghrey. Va Ophelia jannoo y soolagh ass ooylyn veih'n garey. Ta soolagh ooyl millish, agh t'eh mie son y chorp.

Ayns y thie-glass, va fynney ec Evander. Va berrishyn beggey er y fynney, as va ny berrishyn oohchrooagh, cha nel cruinn. Dagh fastyr, va Evander ushtaghey y fynney. “Ushtee eh dagh laa,” dooyrt Ophelia, “as bee ny berrishyn appaghey dy mie.” Va ny berrishyn oohchrooagh appaghey 'sy ghrian. Hoshiaght v'ad eayney as gyn blass, as eisht v'ad millish. Ta appaghey goaill traa.

Dagh Jedoonee, va Ophelia coagyrey oohyn son y chied bee. Ta shliggan er dagh ooh. Ren Evander ny shligganyn y vrishey as y chur er y garey. “Ta'n shliggan mie son y thalloo,” dooyrt eh. Va'n fynney ushtit dagh fastyr, as va ny shligganyn ec y vun echey.

Lurg shey meeaghyn, hie Evander dys y fer-lhee reesht. Va'n cree echey ny share.

Feyshtyn:
Cre dooyrt y fer-lhee rish Evander?
Dooyrt eh dy lhisagh Evander bee share y ee.
Quoi va gobbraghey 'sy eeasteyraght skeddan?
Va shenn ayr Evander gobbraghey 'sy eeasteyraght.
Cre'n glassrey va Ophelia cur er y voayrd?
Va glassrey aw as duillagyn eayney ec Ophelia.
Cre'n cummey ta er ny berrishyn?
Ta ny berrishyn oohchrooagh, cha nel ad cruinn.
Cre haghyr da ny berrishyn 'sy ghrian?
Va ny berrishyn appaghey 'sy ghrian.
Cre ren Evander lesh ny shligganyn?
Ren eh ny shligganyn y chur er y garey.

lessons.title: Ny craueyn 'sy thie tashtee
lessons.summary: Ottoline Blackwood, a guide at the museum in Douglas, shows a school class with nine-year-old Caspian the bones of the extinct giant deer with its great antlers, explains why rats that gnaw and moths that eat cloth are the museum's enemies, and shows an old shoulder yoke, a mast and a brass bell from the time of the Norse colonisation, and a wooden statue of the Virgin Mary.
lessons.text:
Ta Ottoline Blackwood gobbraghey ayns y thie tashtee ayns Doolish. Er y Jeheiney shoh, haink possan veih scoill vunneydagh dys y thie tashtee. Va Caspian, guilley nuy bleeaney d'eash, ayns y possan.

Hoshiaght, hoilshee Ottoline craueyn mooarey daue. “She craueyn feeaih t'ayn,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n feeaih shoh anvio. Cha nel eh bio ayns boayl erbee 'sy theihll nish. Hooar sleih ny craueyn 'syn ellan roish daa cheead blein. Ta'n feeaih shoh er ve anvio rish mysh jeih thousane blein.”

Va eairk vooar er kione y feeaih. Va'n eairk ny smoo na Caspian hene. “Va eairk er dagh çheu jeh'n chione,” dooyrt Ottoline. “Va'n daa eairk ry-cheilley ny smoo lheead na'n dorrys.”

“Cre'n fa t'eh anvio?” denee Caspian.

“Ta'n seihll er chaghlaa,” dooyrt Ottoline. “Haink biljyn er y thalloo, as cha row ynnyd dy liooar ec y feeaih lesh e eairk vooar.”

Eisht loayr Ottoline mychione noidyn y thie tashtee. “Ta daa noid ain: y roddan as y lhemeen. Ta'n roddan crimmey fuygh as pabyr. Ta roddan abyl crimmey trooid boalley fuygh ayns oie. Ta'n lhemeen beg, agh t'eh gee eaddagh. Ta lhemeenyn abyl eaddagh shenn y stroie. Er-y-fa shen, ta shin jeeaghyn dagh laa son roddanyn as lhemeenyn.”

Ayns y nah hamyr, va quing fuygh. “Va'n quing shoh er mwannal ben,” dooyrt Ottoline, “as va ushtey ny bainney ec dagh kione jeh'n quing. Lesh y quing, va'n ven abyl ram ushtey y hroggal ec y traa cheddin.”

Ayns y çhamyr s'jerree, va croan liauyr fuygh. “She croan lhong t'ayn,” dooyrt Ottoline. “Haink lhongyn veih Norlynn dys yn ellan roish thousane blein. She coloinaghey v'ayn: haink sleih veih Norlynn dy chummal 'syn ellan. Va'n coloinaghey shoh scanshoil ayns shennaghys yn ellan.” Ry-lhiattee rish y croan, va clag jeh prash. Va'n prash buigh as gial. “Ta prash lajer, as cha nel eh goll doo,” dooyrt ee.

Va jalloo fuygh ry-lhiattee rish y dorrys, jalloo ben aeg. “She jalloo y Voidyn Moirrey t'ayn,” dooyrt Ottoline. “Va ram jallooyn jeh'n Voidyn ayns ny shenn agglishyn. Va'n jalloo shoh ayns keeill shenn. Hooar ny roddanyn eh, as ren ad crimmey y chass echey!”

Ren Caspian gearey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa nagh vel y feeaih bio nish?
T'eh anvio, er-y-fa dy row caghlaa 'sy theihll.
Cre va er kione y feeaih?
Va eairk vooar er kione y feeaih.
Cre ta'n roddan crimmey?
Ta'n roddan crimmey fuygh as pabyr.
Cre ta'n lhemeen gee?
Ta'n lhemeen gee eaddagh.
Cre ren ben lesh y quing?
Va'n ven abyl ram ushtey y hroggal lesh y quing.
Cre va ry-lhiattee rish y croan?
Va clag jeh prash ry-lhiattee rish y croan.
Cre'n coloinaghey haink roish thousane blein?
She coloinaghey veih Norlynn v'ayn.
Cre va'n jalloo fuygh?
She jalloo y Voidyn Moirrey v'ayn.

lessons.title: Yn oie roish y teisht
lessons.summary: The night before her science exam, sixteen-year-old Henrietta Kingsley revises with her grandfather Montgomery, a retired chemistry teacher, who links each fact to something she can see: argon in a bulb, salt as an ionic substance, the smell of ammonia, book prices that grow in proportion to the number of books, nodes and vascular tubes in a plant, the poles of a magnet, and the Pole Star, which pulsates like her own heart.
lessons.text:
Ta Henrietta Kingsley shey bleeaney jeig d'eash. Er yn oie shoh, ta teisht oaylleeaght eck er y laa ny lurg. Ta aggle urree. Ta'n shenn ayr eck, Montgomery Kingsley, cummal marish y lught-thie ayns Rhumsaa. V'eh ny ynseyder kemmig rish daeed blein.

“Ta ram reddyn aym dy ynsaghey,” dooyrt Henrietta. “Cha nel mee abyl cooinaghtyn orroo ooilley.”

“Ta'n inçhyn cooinaghtyn er reddyn ta shin fakin,” dooyrt yn shenn ayr. “Lhig dooin fakin dagh red.”

Ghow eh soilshey veih'n voayrd. “Ta gas ayns y soilshey shoh,” dooyrt eh. “She argon y gas. Ta argon ayns yn aer, myrgeddin: ta mysh un ayrn jeh argon ayns keead ayrn jeh'n aer. Cha nel argon jannoo red erbee lesh stooghyn elley, as er-y-fa shen t'eh mie son soilshaghyn.”

Eisht ghow eh sollan. “Ta sollan ny stoo eeaneagh,” dooyrt eh. “Ta kiangley eeaneagh ayn eddyr daa vunstoo. Tra ta sollan ayns ushtey, ta ny paartyn eeaneagh goll veih y cheilley.”

Eisht hug Montgomery stoo glenney faggys da stroin Henrietta. Hug ee e laue er e stroin. “She ammoiney t'ayn,” dooyrt eh. “Ta soar lajer ec ammoiney, as ta sleih jannoo ymmyd jeh ammoiney son glenney.”

Eisht, va red coreiragh dy ynsaghey. “Jeeagh,” dooyrt Montgomery. “My ta un lioar queig puint, ta daa lioar jeih puint, as ta three lioaryn queig puint jeig. Ta'n costys coreiragh rish earroo ny lioaryn. Tra ta un red goll daa cheayrt cho mooar, as ta'n red elley goll daa cheayrt cho mooar myrgeddin, ta ny reddyn coreiragh.”

Ghow eh lus veih'n voayrd. “Ta lus cuishlagh ayn shoh. Ta'n lus cuishlagh cur ushtey trooid y lus, veih ny fraueyn gys ny duillagyn. Jeeagh er ny noadyn er y lus: ec dagh noad, ta duillag gaase.”

Eisht hie ad magh. Va clagh vagnaidagh ayns laue Montgomery. “Ta daa phoull ec dagh clagh vagnaidagh: poull twoaie as poull jiass,” dooyrt eh. “As ta daa phoull ec y theihll myrgeddin.” Hoilshee eh rollage di. “Ta'n rollage shoh harrish y Poull Hwoaie. She rollage vuillagh ee: t'ee goll ny smoo as ny sloo, myr dty chree buillagh.”

Hug Henrietta e laue er e chree. Va'n cree buillagh. Ren ee gearey. Laa ny lurg, ren ee y teisht, as va dy chooilley red ayns e kione.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n gas ta ayns y soilshey?
She argon y gas ayns y soilshey.
Cre'n sorçh dy stoo ta sollan?
Ta sollan ny stoo eeaneagh.
Cre ta sleih jannoo lesh ammoiney?
Ta sleih jannoo ymmyd jeh ammoiney son glenney.
Cre ta'n lus cuishlagh jannoo lesh ushtey?
Ta'n lus cuishlagh cur ushtey veih ny fraueyn gys ny duillagyn.
Cre ta gaase ec dagh noad?
Ec dagh noad, ta duillag gaase.
Cre'n sorçh dy rollage ta harrish y Poull Hwoaie?
She rollage vuillagh ee.
